title: Optical Momentum Lab: Lens Refraction & Elastic Collisions
description: A physics sandbox where ShaderBall2 objects roll along a curved ramp and collide with the SunglassesKhronos model, which acts as a refractive lens gate. Users adjust lens curvature, ball mass, launch velocity, and surface friction to study conservation of momentum and energy through elastic and inelastic collision modes, with full undo/redo of every parameter change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load SunglassesKhronos.glb and place it at center as a 'lens gate' on a pedestal. Load ShaderBall2.glb and clone it to create up to 3 launcher balls positioned on a curved ramp to the left. Scene setup: PerspectiveCamera at (0,4,10), ambient light intensity 0.4, one directional light from (5,8,5) casting shadows, a ground plane with grid texture, and a subtle environment map for reflections. Physics interactions (implement manually, no library): (1) A velocity slider (1-20 m/s) sets launch speed of the selected ball. (2) A mass slider (0.5-5 kg) per ball changes its mass, visually scaling the ShaderBall2 clone. (3) A friction coefficient slider (0-1) affects deceleration on the ramp. (4) A 'lens curvature' slider (0.5-2.0) warps the sunglasses model scale on X-axis, changing the deflection angle applied to balls passing through. (5) A toggle between elastic and inelastic collision mode. (6) A 'Launch' button fires the selected ball down the ramp toward the sunglasses gate. Balls passing through the lens gate get deflected based on curvature value and continue to the right side where they can collide with previously launched balls. Display a real-time HUD showing total kinetic energy and total momentum of the system to verify conservation laws. Implement full undo/redo: every slider change, mode toggle, and launch is pushed onto a history stack. Ctrl+Z undoes the last action (reverting slider values and removing launched balls), Ctrl+Y redoes. A ball selector (buttons labeled Ball 1-3) chooses which ball to configure and launch next. Animate balls with requestAnimationFrame, applying velocity, friction deceleration, lens deflection angle, and collision response using conservation of momentum equations. Show velocity vectors as colored arrows on each moving ball. Total required interaction steps: select ball, set mass, set velocity, set friction, set lens curvature, choose collision mode, launch, repeat for second ball, observe collision, undo a step, redo it, adjust curvature and relaunch.
